en: The Pair on What is to be Abandoned by Cultivation (Bhāvanāyapahātabbaduka)
Dependent on a state to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāya pahātabba*), a state not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state to be abandoned by cultivation, a state not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state to be abandoned by cultivation, a state both not to be abandoned by cultivation and not not to be abandoned by cultivation [arises]...
And states arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not to be abandoned by cultivation, a state not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a state to be abandoned by cultivation and a state not to be abandoned by cultivation, a state not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition.
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the ripening condition, one ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.
